cards.text: Quick catch-up, friend: Paul, the apostle, has been on trial in Caesarea before Festus, the Roman governor who took over from Felix, and Paul just said, 'I appeal to Caesar!' Several days later, King Agrippa and Bernice come down to Caesarea. Royalty, in the BUILDING.

cards.question: Why do King Agrippa and Bernice come down to Caesarea?

answers.text: To pay their respects to Festus
To collect taxes from the city
To celebrate a feast in the city

cards.text: They're staying several days. Several! That's not a visit, that's a HOUSEGUEST situation. So Festus brings up work: a man that Felix left in prison.
Festus says that while he was in Jerusalem, the chief priests and elders of the Jews laid out their case against this man. They wanted a judgment against him.

cards.question: Festus told them it's not the Roman custom to hand a man over before he can face his ___ and ___ himself against their charges.
Back in Caesarea, Festus waited a few weeks before hearing Paul's case.
Festus says that when Paul's accusers rose to speak, they charged him with the crimes he had expected.

cards.text: I bet Festus was braced for theft, riots, maybe a little tax fraud. Instead he gets arguments about their own religion and 'a certain Jesus who had died.'

cards.question: Festus says the arguments were about a certain Jesus who had died, but whom Paul said was ___.
Festus tells Agrippa why he asked Paul about going to Jerusalem to be tried there. What reason does he give?

answers.text: He was at a loss how to investigate
He was afraid of a riot in Caesarea
He had to report to Jerusalem anyway

cards.question: Since Paul appealed to the Emperor, Festus says he ordered Paul held until he could send him to Caesar.
After all that, King Agrippa has a request for Festus about Paul. What is it?

answers.text: To have him released at once
To send him back to Felix

cards.question: Festus promises Agrippa he'll hear Paul tomorrow. The next day, Agrippa and Bernice slip into the auditorium quietly with no fuss.

cards.text: In they come with great pomp, along with the commanders and the city's leading men, and Festus orders Paul brought in. Last grand entrance anybody made for ME was the junk drawer sliding open so somebody could grab a RUBBER BAND.

cards.question: Festus tells the room the whole Jewish community has petitioned him about Paul, both in Caesarea and in Jerusalem. What were they crying out?

answers.text: That he ought not to live any longer
That he should be sent to Rome
That he should be whipped and released

cards.question: Festus tells the crowd he found Paul had done nothing worthy of death.
Festus says he has a problem with sending Paul on to the Emperor. What is it?

answers.text: He has nothing definite to write
He has no ship to send him on
The Emperor refuses to see prisoners

cards.question: Festus says it seems unreasonable to send on a prisoner without specifying the ___ against him.

cards.text: So Festus is trying HARD not to ship a prisoner to the Emperor with a note that says, 'No idea. Good luck.' And that's where we'll pause, friend, because King Agrippa hasn't heard one word from Paul yet.

findings.problem: Bernice appears here for the first time but is never introduced. The card only names her next to King Agrippa, so the baker isn't told who she is.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The question says Festus 'promises' Agrippa he'll hear Paul tomorrow. The text says Festus 'declared' it (Acts 25:22). Calling it a promise relabels what the text calls it.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The card mostly recaps cards 17 and 18: Festus has nothing definite to write and doesn't want to send a prisoner without charges. It never tells the key new detail in Acts 25:26: Festus has brought Paul before all of them, especially King Agrippa, so that after this inquiry he may have something to write. That detail is why the hearing is happening, and it is never told or asked on any card.

The purpose of the hearing in Acts 25:26 (Paul is brought before all of them, especially King Agrippa, so Festus will have something to write after the inquiry) is an important detail that the walkthrough leaves out.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: From card 10 on, the question types settle into a back-and-forth between multiple choice and true or false: MC (10), TF (11), MC (12), TF (13), then MC (15), TF (16), MC (17). That reads as a pattern rather than a natural choice for each card.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern.
